title: All Employees
prompt: Return ALL columns from the Employees table.
hint: Use SELECT * FROM table_name to retrieve every column. The asterisk (*) is a wildcard meaning 'all columns'.
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Employees;

title: Employee Names
prompt: Show only the name column from Employees.
hint: Instead of *, list the specific column name after SELECT. Syntax: SELECT column_name FROM table;
expectedQuery: SELECT name FROM Employees;

title: Name and Salary
prompt: Show the name and salary columns from Employees.
hint: Separate multiple column names with commas: SELECT col1, col2 FROM table;
expectedQuery: SELECT name, salary FROM Employees;

title: All Products
prompt: Return all columns from the Products table.
hint: Use SELECT * FROM Products; — the asterisk retrieves every column in the table.
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Products;

title: Unique Cities
prompt: Show all unique cities from the Customers table (no duplicates).
hint: SELECT DISTINCT column_name removes duplicate values from the result. Apply it to the city column.
expectedQuery: SELECT DISTINCT city FROM Customers;

title: Column Alias
prompt: Show employee names with the column header displayed as 'employee_name'.
hint: Use AS to rename a column in output: SELECT column AS alias_name FROM table;
expectedQuery: SELECT name AS employee_name FROM Employees;

title: Select Literal Value
prompt: Write a query that returns the text 'Hello SQL' as a column called greeting.
hint: You can SELECT literal values directly: SELECT 'some text' AS column_name; — no FROM clause needed.
expectedQuery: SELECT 'Hello SQL' AS greeting;

title: Computed Column
prompt: Show each product's name and its price multiplied by 2, labeled as 'double_price'.
hint: You can perform arithmetic in SELECT: SELECT name, price * 2 AS double_price FROM Products;
expectedQuery: SELECT name, price * 2 AS double_price FROM Products;

title: High Salary
prompt: Find employees earning more than 60000.
hint: Use WHERE to filter rows: SELECT * FROM Employees WHERE salary > 60000; The > operator means 'greater than'.
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Employees WHERE salary > 60000;

title: Exact Match
prompt: Find the employee named 'Alice'.
hint: Use = for exact match: WHERE name = 'Alice'. Text values must be in single quotes.
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Employees WHERE name = 'Alice';

title: Not Equal
prompt: Show all departments except 'Sales'.
hint: Use != or <> for 'not equal': WHERE name != 'Sales' filters out rows that match.
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Departments WHERE name != 'Sales';

title: Less Than
prompt: Find products priced under 100.
hint: Use < for 'less than': WHERE price < 100 returns only rows where price is below 100.
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Products WHERE price < 100;

title: AND Condition
prompt: Find employees in department 1 who earn more than 70000.
hint: Combine conditions with AND — both must be true: WHERE department_id = 1 AND salary > 70000
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Employees WHERE department_id = 1 AND salary > 70000;

title: OR Condition
prompt: Find customers from Berlin or Paris.
hint: Use OR when either condition can be true: WHERE city = 'Berlin' OR city = 'Paris'
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Customers WHERE city = 'Berlin' OR city = 'Paris';

title: NOT Condition
prompt: Find all employees NOT in department 2.
hint: NOT reverses a condition: WHERE NOT department_id = 2. Alternatively: WHERE department_id != 2
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Employees WHERE NOT department_id = 2;

title: Combined Conditions
prompt: Find products that cost at least 100 and are in stock (in_stock = 1).
hint: Combine with AND: WHERE price >= 100 AND in_stock = 1. The >= operator means 'greater than or equal to'.
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Products WHERE price >= 100 AND in_stock = 1;

title: Find NULLs
prompt: Find employees who have no department assigned (department_id is NULL).
hint: NULL is special — you cannot use = NULL. Instead use IS NULL: WHERE department_id IS NULL
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Employees WHERE department_id IS NULL;

title: Exclude NULLs
prompt: Show products that have a category assigned (category_id is NOT NULL).
hint: Use IS NOT NULL to filter out rows with missing values: WHERE category_id IS NOT NULL
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Products WHERE category_id IS NOT NULL;

title: Customers With Age
prompt: Find customers whose age is known (not NULL).
hint: Use WHERE age IS NOT NULL to exclude rows where the age value is missing.
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Customers WHERE age IS NOT NULL;

title: COALESCE Basics
prompt: Show each employee's name and department_id, replacing NULL department_id with 0.
hint: COALESCE(value, default) returns the first non-NULL argument. Use COALESCE(department_id, 0) to substitute 0 for NULLs.
expectedQuery: SELECT name, COALESCE(department_id, 0) AS department_id FROM Employees;

title: COALESCE With Text
prompt: Show customer names and their age, displaying 'Unknown' when age is NULL.
hint: COALESCE works with text too: COALESCE(age, 'Unknown'). It picks the first non-NULL value from the list.
expectedQuery: SELECT name, COALESCE(age, 'Unknown') AS age FROM Customers;

title: First 5 Employees
prompt: Show only the first 5 employees.
hint: Add LIMIT n at the end of your query to restrict the number of returned rows: SELECT * FROM table LIMIT 5;
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Employees LIMIT 5;

title: Top 3 Products by Price
prompt: Show the 3 most expensive products.
hint: First ORDER BY price DESC to sort highest first, then LIMIT 3 to get the top three.
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Products ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 3;

title: Skip and Take
prompt: Show employees 4 through 6 (skip the first 3, then take 3).
hint: LIMIT count OFFSET skip — LIMIT 3 OFFSET 3 skips the first 3 rows and returns the next 3.
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Employees LIMIT 3 OFFSET 3;

title: Single Row
prompt: Show just one customer from the Customers table.
hint: LIMIT 1 restricts the output to a single row. Useful for peeking at table structure.
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Customers LIMIT 1;

title: Unique Countries
prompt: List all unique countries from the Customers table.
hint: SELECT DISTINCT country FROM Customers; removes duplicate country values from the result.
expectedQuery: SELECT DISTINCT country FROM Customers;

title: Unique Departments
prompt: List all unique department_id values from Employees (include NULLs).
hint: DISTINCT includes NULL as a unique value. SELECT DISTINCT department_id FROM Employees; will show all unique values including NULL.
expectedQuery: SELECT DISTINCT department_id FROM Employees;

title: Unique City-Country Pairs
prompt: Show all unique combinations of city and country from Customers.
hint: DISTINCT can apply to multiple columns: SELECT DISTINCT city, country FROM table; treats each combination as unique.
expectedQuery: SELECT DISTINCT city, country FROM Customers;

title: Price After Tax
prompt: Show each product's name and price with 20% tax added, labeled 'price_with_tax'.
hint: Multiply by 1.2 to add 20%: SELECT name, price * 1.2 AS price_with_tax FROM Products;
expectedQuery: SELECT name, price * 1.2 AS price_with_tax FROM Products;

title: Salary Difference
prompt: Show old_salary, new_salary, and the difference (new minus old) as 'raise' from EmployeeHistory.
hint: Subtract columns: new_salary - old_salary. Use AS to name the result column 'raise'.
expectedQuery: SELECT old_salary, new_salary, new_salary - old_salary AS raise FROM EmployeeHistory;

title: Half Price Sale
prompt: Show product names and their price divided by 2 as 'sale_price'.
hint: Use the division operator /: SELECT name, price / 2 AS sale_price FROM Products;
expectedQuery: SELECT name, price / 2 AS sale_price FROM Products;

title: Order Total
prompt: Show order id and the total value (quantity * product price) for each order. Join Orders with Products.
hint: Join the tables and multiply: SELECT Orders.id, Orders.quantity * Products.price AS total FROM Orders JOIN Products ON Orders.product_id = Products.id;
expectedQuery: SELECT Orders.id, Orders.quantity * Products.price AS total FROM Orders JOIN Products ON Orders.product_id = Products.id;

title: Uppercase Names
prompt: Show all customer names in uppercase.
hint: UPPER(text) converts text to uppercase: SELECT UPPER(name) FROM Customers;
expectedQuery: SELECT UPPER(name) FROM Customers;

title: Lowercase Cities
prompt: Show all customer cities in lowercase.
hint: LOWER(text) converts to lowercase: SELECT LOWER(city) FROM Customers;
expectedQuery: SELECT LOWER(city) FROM Customers;

title: Name Length
prompt: Show each employee's name and the length of their name as 'name_length'.
hint: LENGTH(text) returns the number of characters: SELECT name, LENGTH(name) AS name_length FROM Employees;
expectedQuery: SELECT name, LENGTH(name) AS name_length FROM Employees;

title: First Three Letters
prompt: Show the first 3 characters of each department name as 'short_name'.
hint: SUBSTR(text, start, length) extracts a substring. Start position is 1-based: SUBSTR(name, 1, 3)
expectedQuery: SELECT SUBSTR(name, 1, 3) AS short_name FROM Departments;

title: Replace Text
prompt: Show customer emails with '@mail.com' replaced by '@email.org'.
hint: REPLACE(text, old, new) substitutes occurrences: REPLACE(email, '@mail.com', '@email.org')
expectedQuery: SELECT REPLACE(email, '@mail.com', '@email.org') FROM Customers;

title: Concatenation
prompt: Show each employee's name and email combined as 'Name <email>' using the format: name || ' <' || email || '>'.
hint: The || operator concatenates strings in SQLite: 'Hello' || ' ' || 'World' produces 'Hello World'.
expectedQuery: SELECT name || ' <' || email || '>' AS contact FROM Employees;

title: Check Types
prompt: Show each product's name and the type of its price column using TYPEOF().
hint: TYPEOF(value) returns the storage type as a string ('integer', 'text', 'real', 'null', 'blob').
expectedQuery: SELECT name, TYPEOF(price) FROM Products;

title: Cast to Text
prompt: Show each employee's salary converted to text using CAST, as 'salary_text'.
hint: CAST(value AS type) converts between types: CAST(salary AS TEXT) turns the number into a text string.
expectedQuery: SELECT name, CAST(salary AS TEXT) AS salary_text FROM Employees;

title: Cast to Real
prompt: Show each product's name and price cast as REAL (floating point) as 'price_real'.
hint: CAST(price AS REAL) converts an integer to a floating-point number, enabling decimal division results.
expectedQuery: SELECT name, CAST(price AS REAL) AS price_real FROM Products;

title: Add a Department
prompt: Insert a new department with id 6 and name 'Legal' into the Departments table.
hint: Use INSERT INTO table VALUES(val1, val2) to add a row. Syntax: INSERT INTO Departments VALUES(6, 'Legal');
expectedQuery: INSERT INTO Departments VALUES(6, 'Legal');
verificationQuery: SELECT * FROM Departments ORDER BY id;

title: Add a Customer
prompt: Insert a new customer: id=9, name='Nina', city='Vienna', country='Austria', email='nina@mail.com', age=27.
hint: List all values in the same order as the columns: INSERT INTO Customers VALUES(9, 'Nina', 'Vienna', 'Austria', 'nina@mail.com', 27);
expectedQuery: INSERT INTO Customers VALUES(9, 'Nina', 'Vienna', 'Austria', 'nina@mail.com', 27);
verificationQuery: SELECT * FROM Customers ORDER BY id;

title: Add Multiple Products
prompt: Insert two new products: (11, 'Tablet', 500, 1, 1) and (12, 'Charger', 30, 5, 1).
hint: Insert multiple rows in one statement by separating value groups with commas: INSERT INTO table VALUES(...), (...);
expectedQuery: INSERT INTO Products VALUES(11, 'Tablet', 500, 1, 1), (12, 'Charger', 30, 5, 1);
verificationQuery: SELECT * FROM Products ORDER BY id;

title: Insert With Named Columns
prompt: Insert a supplier with id=5 and name='QuickShip'. Set country to 'Canada' and rating to 3. Use explicit column names.
hint: Specify columns: INSERT INTO Suppliers(id, name, country, rating) VALUES(5, 'QuickShip', 'Canada', 3);
expectedQuery: INSERT INTO Suppliers(id, name, country, rating) VALUES(5, 'QuickShip', 'Canada', 3);
verificationQuery: SELECT * FROM Suppliers ORDER BY id;

title: Insert With NULL
prompt: Insert a product with id=11, name='Cable', price=15, no category (NULL), and in_stock=1.
hint: Use NULL (without quotes) for missing values: INSERT INTO Products VALUES(11, 'Cable', 15, NULL, 1);
expectedQuery: INSERT INTO Products VALUES(11, 'Cable', 15, NULL, 1);
verificationQuery: SELECT * FROM Products ORDER BY id;

title: Delete One Row
prompt: Delete the customer with id 8 from the Customers table.
hint: DELETE FROM table WHERE condition; removes matching rows. Use WHERE id = 8 to target one specific row.
expectedQuery: DELETE FROM Customers WHERE id = 8;
verificationQuery: SELECT * FROM Customers ORDER BY id;

title: Delete by Condition
prompt: Delete all products that are not in stock (in_stock = 0).
hint: DELETE FROM Products WHERE in_stock = 0; removes all rows matching the condition. Always use WHERE to avoid deleting everything!
expectedQuery: DELETE FROM Products WHERE in_stock = 0;
verificationQuery: SELECT * FROM Products ORDER BY id;

title: Delete All Rows
prompt: Delete ALL rows from the EmployeeHistory table.
hint: DELETE FROM table_name; without a WHERE clause removes every row. The table still exists but is empty.
expectedQuery: DELETE FROM EmployeeHistory;
verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM EmployeeHistory;

title: Delete Low-Rated Suppliers
prompt: Delete suppliers with a rating below 4.
hint: Use WHERE rating < 4 to target low-rated suppliers. DELETE FROM Suppliers WHERE rating < 4;
expectedQuery: DELETE FROM Suppliers WHERE rating < 4;
verificationQuery: SELECT * FROM Suppliers ORDER BY id;

title: Sort by Name
prompt: Show all employees sorted by name alphabetically (A-Z).
hint: ORDER BY column_name sorts ascending by default (A-Z for text). Place it after the FROM/WHERE clause.
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Employees ORDER BY name;

title: Sort Descending
prompt: Show all products ordered by price from highest to lowest.
hint: Add DESC after the column name to sort in descending order: ORDER BY price DESC
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Products ORDER BY price DESC;

title: Multi-Column Sort
prompt: Show all customers sorted by country ascending, then by name ascending.
hint: Separate multiple sort columns with commas: ORDER BY country, name. The first column is the primary sort.
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Customers ORDER BY country, name;

title: Sort by Expression
prompt: Show employee names and salaries, sorted by salary divided by 1000 descending.
hint: You can ORDER BY an expression: ORDER BY salary / 1000 DESC. The expression is computed per row for sorting.
expectedQuery: SELECT name, salary FROM Employees ORDER BY salary / 1000 DESC;

title: Sort by Column Number
prompt: Show product name and price, sorted by the second column (price) ascending.
hint: You can reference columns by position: ORDER BY 2 means sort by the second column in the SELECT list.
expectedQuery: SELECT name, price FROM Products ORDER BY 2;

title: Top 5 Salaries
prompt: Show the 5 highest-paid employees (name and salary only).
hint: Combine ORDER BY salary DESC with LIMIT 5 to get the top earners.
expectedQuery: SELECT name, salary FROM Employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 5;

title: Starts With M
prompt: Find customers whose name starts with 'M'.
hint: LIKE 'M%' matches any string starting with M. The % wildcard represents zero or more characters.
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Customers WHERE name LIKE 'M%';

title: Ends With a
prompt: Find employees whose name ends with the letter 'a'.
hint: Use '%a' to match names ending with 'a'. The % before 'a' matches any characters preceding it.
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Employees WHERE name LIKE '%a';

title: Contains 'an'
prompt: Find employees whose name contains 'an' anywhere.
hint: Use '%an%' — the % on both sides means 'an' can appear anywhere in the string.
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Employees WHERE name LIKE '%an%';

title: Single Character Wildcard
prompt: Find products whose name has exactly 5 characters.
hint: The underscore _ matches exactly one character. Five underscores _____ matches any 5-character string: WHERE name LIKE '_____'
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Products WHERE name LIKE '_____';

title: NOT LIKE
prompt: Find all customers whose city does NOT start with 'B'.
hint: NOT LIKE reverses the pattern match: WHERE city NOT LIKE 'B%' excludes cities starting with B.
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Customers WHERE city NOT LIKE 'B%';

title: Email Domain Search
prompt: Find customers whose email ends with '@mail.com'.
hint: Use LIKE '%@mail.com' to find emails ending with that domain. The % matches everything before the @.
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Customers WHERE email LIKE '%@mail.com';

title: Cities List
prompt: Find customers from Berlin, Paris, or Tokyo.
hint: IN (val1, val2, val3) checks if a value matches any in the list. Shorter than multiple OR conditions.
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Customers WHERE city IN ('Berlin', 'Paris', 'Tokyo');

title: Department Filter
prompt: Find employees in departments 1, 3, or 5.
hint: WHERE department_id IN (1, 3, 5) is equivalent to department_id = 1 OR department_id = 3 OR department_id = 5
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Employees WHERE department_id IN (1, 3, 5);

title: NOT IN
prompt: Find products NOT in categories 1 or 2.
hint: NOT IN excludes matching values: WHERE category_id NOT IN (1, 2). Note: NULLs are not matched by NOT IN.
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Products WHERE category_id NOT IN (1, 2);

title: Payment Methods
prompt: Show payments made via 'PayPal' or 'Debit Card'.
hint: Use IN to match multiple text values: WHERE method IN ('PayPal', 'Debit Card')
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Payments WHERE method IN ('PayPal', 'Debit Card');

title: Supplier Countries
prompt: Show suppliers from 'USA' or 'France'.
hint: WHERE country IN ('USA', 'France') matches suppliers from either country.
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Suppliers WHERE country IN ('USA', 'France');

title: Price Range
prompt: Find products priced between 50 and 200 (inclusive).
hint: BETWEEN includes both boundaries: WHERE price BETWEEN 50 AND 200 means price >= 50 AND price <= 200.
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Products WHERE price BETWEEN 50 AND 200;

title: Salary Range
prompt: Find employees with salaries between 50000 and 80000.
hint: BETWEEN works with any comparable values: WHERE salary BETWEEN 50000 AND 80000
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Employees WHERE salary BETWEEN 50000 AND 80000;

title: Date Range
prompt: Find orders placed between '2024-02-01' and '2024-03-31'.
hint: BETWEEN works with date strings too: WHERE order_date BETWEEN '2024-02-01' AND '2024-03-31'. Dates are compared lexicographically in SQLite.
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Orders WHERE order_date BETWEEN '2024-02-01' AND '2024-03-31';

title: NOT BETWEEN
prompt: Find products NOT priced between 100 and 500.
hint: NOT BETWEEN excludes the range: WHERE price NOT BETWEEN 100 AND 500 returns items outside that range.
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Products WHERE price NOT BETWEEN 100 AND 500;

title: Column Alias
prompt: Show employee names as 'full_name' and salary as 'annual_pay'.
hint: Use AS to rename columns in output: SELECT name AS full_name, salary AS annual_pay FROM Employees;
expectedQuery: SELECT name AS full_name, salary AS annual_pay FROM Employees;

title: Table Alias
prompt: Show employee names and department_ids using 'e' as a table alias for Employees.
hint: Table aliases shorten queries: SELECT e.name, e.department_id FROM Employees e; or FROM Employees AS e
expectedQuery: SELECT e.name, e.department_id FROM Employees AS e;

title: Expression Alias
prompt: Show each product's name and price * 0.9 as 'discounted_price'.
hint: Alias any expression: SELECT name, price * 0.9 AS discounted_price FROM Products;
expectedQuery: SELECT name, price * 0.9 AS discounted_price FROM Products;

title: Multiple Table Aliases
prompt: Show order id and customer name using aliases 'o' for Orders and 'c' for Customers.
hint: When joining tables, aliases make queries readable: FROM Orders AS o JOIN Customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.id
expectedQuery: SELECT o.id, c.name FROM Orders AS o JOIN Customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.id;

title: Count All Employees
prompt: Count the total number of employees.
hint: COUNT(*) counts all rows including NULLs: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Employees;
expectedQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Employees;

title: Count Non-NULL
prompt: Count how many employees have a department_id assigned (not NULL).
hint: COUNT(column) only counts non-NULL values: COUNT(department_id) skips rows where department_id is NULL.
expectedQuery: SELECT COUNT(department_id) FROM Employees;

title: Total Salary
prompt: Calculate the total salary bill (sum of all salaries) from Employees.
hint: SUM(column) adds up all values: SELECT SUM(salary) FROM Employees;
expectedQuery: SELECT SUM(salary) FROM Employees;

title: Average Price
prompt: Calculate the average price of all products.
hint: AVG(column) computes the arithmetic mean: SELECT AVG(price) FROM Products;
expectedQuery: SELECT AVG(price) FROM Products;

title: Min and Max Salary
prompt: Show the minimum and maximum salary from Employees.
hint: MIN(column) and MAX(column) find extremes: SELECT MIN(salary), MAX(salary) FROM Employees;
expectedQuery: SELECT MIN(salary), MAX(salary) FROM Employees;

title: Count Distinct
prompt: Count the number of distinct cities in the Customers table.
hint: COUNT(DISTINCT column) counts unique non-NULL values: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT city) FROM Customers;
expectedQuery: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT city) FROM Customers;

title: Max Product Price
prompt: Find the most expensive product's price, labeled as 'highest_price'.
hint: Use MAX with an alias: SELECT MAX(price) AS highest_price FROM Products;
expectedQuery: SELECT MAX(price) AS highest_price FROM Products;

title: Total Order Quantity
prompt: Calculate the total quantity of all orders combined.
hint: SUM works on any numeric column: SELECT SUM(quantity) FROM Orders;
expectedQuery: SELECT SUM(quantity) FROM Orders;

title: Employee Departments
prompt: Show employee names with their department names.
hint: JOIN connects two tables on a related column: FROM Employees JOIN Departments ON Employees.department_id = Departments.id
expectedQuery: SELECT Employees.name, Departments.name FROM Employees JOIN Departments ON Employees.department_id = Departments.id;

title: Order Details
prompt: Show order id, customer name, and product name for each order.
hint: Join three tables: Orders → Customers (on customer_id) and Orders → Products (on product_id).
expectedQuery: SELECT Orders.id, Customers.name, Products.name FROM Orders JOIN Customers ON Orders.customer_id = Customers.id JOIN Products ON Orders.product_id = Products.id;

title: Product Categories
prompt: Show product names with their category names.
hint: JOIN Products and Categories on the category_id: FROM Products JOIN Categories ON Products.category_id = Categories.id
expectedQuery: SELECT Products.name, Categories.name FROM Products JOIN Categories ON Products.category_id = Categories.id;

title: JOIN with Alias
prompt: Show employee name and department name using table aliases e and d.
hint: Use short aliases: FROM Employees AS e JOIN Departments AS d ON e.department_id = d.id
expectedQuery: SELECT e.name, d.name FROM Employees AS e JOIN Departments AS d ON e.department_id = d.id;

title: JOIN with WHERE
prompt: Show names of employees in the 'Engineering' department.
hint: After JOIN, add WHERE to filter: JOIN Departments ON ... WHERE Departments.name = 'Engineering'
expectedQuery: SELECT Employees.name FROM Employees JOIN Departments ON Employees.department_id = Departments.id WHERE Departments.name = 'Engineering';

title: Inventory with Products
prompt: Show product names and their stock levels from Inventory.
hint: JOIN Inventory and Products on product_id: FROM Inventory JOIN Products ON Inventory.product_id = Products.id
expectedQuery: SELECT Products.name, Inventory.stock FROM Inventory JOIN Products ON Inventory.product_id = Products.id;

title: Payments with Customers
prompt: Show customer name and payment amount for all payments.
hint: JOIN Payments with Customers on customer_id to connect payment records with customer names.
expectedQuery: SELECT Customers.name, Payments.amount FROM Payments JOIN Customers ON Payments.customer_id = Customers.id;

title: Assignments with Details
prompt: Show employee name, project name, and role from Assignments.
hint: Join Assignments to both Employees (on employee_id) and Projects (on project_id) to get the names.
expectedQuery: SELECT Employees.name, Projects.name, Assignments.role FROM Assignments JOIN Employees ON Assignments.employee_id = Employees.id JOIN Projects ON Assignments.project_id = Projects.id;

title: Update Single Column
prompt: Change Alice's salary to 80000.
hint: UPDATE table SET column = value WHERE condition; — always include WHERE to avoid updating all rows!
expectedQuery: UPDATE Employees SET salary = 80000 WHERE name = 'Alice';
verificationQuery: SELECT name, salary FROM Employees WHERE name = 'Alice';

title: Update Multiple Columns
prompt: Update customer John: set city to 'Munich' and age to 36.
hint: SET multiple columns with commas: UPDATE Customers SET city = 'Munich', age = 36 WHERE name = 'John';
expectedQuery: UPDATE Customers SET city = 'Munich', age = 36 WHERE name = 'John';
verificationQuery: SELECT name, city, age FROM Customers WHERE name = 'John';

title: Raise All Salaries
prompt: Give every employee a 10% raise (multiply salary by 1.1).
hint: Omit WHERE to update all rows. Use arithmetic: UPDATE Employees SET salary = salary * 1.1;
expectedQuery: UPDATE Employees SET salary = salary * 1.1;
verificationQuery: SELECT name, salary FROM Employees ORDER BY id;

title: Update With Condition
prompt: Set in_stock to 0 for all products priced above 500.
hint: UPDATE Products SET in_stock = 0 WHERE price > 500; targets only expensive products.
expectedQuery: UPDATE Products SET in_stock = 0 WHERE price > 500;
verificationQuery: SELECT name, price, in_stock FROM Products ORDER BY id;

title: Update With Arithmetic
prompt: Double the stock of all inventory items.
hint: Use SET stock = stock * 2 to multiply existing values. This updates each row based on its current value.
expectedQuery: UPDATE Inventory SET stock = stock * 2;
verificationQuery: SELECT * FROM Inventory ORDER BY product_id, supplier_id;

title: Set NULL Value
prompt: Set George's department_id to 2 (he was previously unassigned).
hint: UPDATE to replace a NULL with a value: UPDATE Employees SET department_id = 2 WHERE name = 'George';
expectedQuery: UPDATE Employees SET department_id = 2 WHERE name = 'George';
verificationQuery: SELECT name, department_id FROM Employees WHERE name = 'George';

title: Employees Per Department
prompt: Count employees in each department.
hint: GROUP BY creates groups. SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) FROM Employees GROUP BY department_id;
expectedQuery: SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) FROM Employees GROUP BY department_id;

title: Total Sales by Region
prompt: Show total quantity_sold per region from SalesLog.
hint: SUM with GROUP BY: SELECT region, SUM(quantity_sold) FROM SalesLog GROUP BY region;
expectedQuery: SELECT region, SUM(quantity_sold) FROM SalesLog GROUP BY region;

title: Average Salary by Dept
prompt: Show the average salary per department_id.
hint: AVG inside a GROUP BY: SELECT department_id, AVG(salary) FROM Employees GROUP BY department_id;
expectedQuery: SELECT department_id, AVG(salary) FROM Employees GROUP BY department_id;

title: Orders per Customer
prompt: Count the number of orders each customer has placed.
hint: GROUP BY customer_id with COUNT(*): SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) FROM Orders GROUP BY customer_id;
expectedQuery: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) FROM Orders GROUP BY customer_id;

title: Products per Category
prompt: Count products in each category.
hint: SELECT category_id, COUNT(*) FROM Products GROUP BY category_id; — NULL categories form their own group.
expectedQuery: SELECT category_id, COUNT(*) FROM Products GROUP BY category_id;

title: Salary Label
prompt: Show employee names with a label: 'High' if salary > 70000, otherwise 'Standard'.
hint: CASE WHEN condition THEN result ELSE default END — use it in SELECT to create computed labels.
expectedQuery: SELECT name, CASE WHEN salary > 70000 THEN 'High' ELSE 'Standard' END AS salary_level FROM Employees;

title: Stock Status
prompt: Show product names with 'Available' if in_stock = 1, 'Out of Stock' otherwise.
hint: CASE WHEN in_stock = 1 THEN 'Available' ELSE 'Out of Stock' END — transforms numeric flags into readable labels.
expectedQuery: SELECT name, CASE WHEN in_stock = 1 THEN 'Available' ELSE 'Out of Stock' END AS status FROM Products;

title: Price Tier
prompt: Label products as 'Budget' (price < 50), 'Mid' (50-200), or 'Premium' (> 200).
hint: Chain multiple WHEN clauses: CASE WHEN price < 50 THEN 'Budget' WHEN price <= 200 THEN 'Mid' ELSE 'Premium' END
expectedQuery: SELECT name, CASE WHEN price < 50 THEN 'Budget' WHEN price <= 200 THEN 'Mid' ELSE 'Premium' END AS tier FROM Products;

title: Rating Stars
prompt: Show supplier names with their rating as text: 5='Excellent', 4='Good', 3='Average', else 'Below Average'.
hint: Use CASE with specific values: CASE rating WHEN 5 THEN 'Excellent' WHEN 4 THEN 'Good' ... END — this is the 'simple CASE' form.
expectedQuery: SELECT name, CASE rating WHEN 5 THEN 'Excellent' WHEN 4 THEN 'Good' WHEN 3 THEN 'Average' ELSE 'Below Average' END AS rating_text FROM Suppliers;

title: Customers With Orders
prompt: Find customers who have placed at least one order.
hint: EXISTS checks if a subquery returns any rows: WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Orders WHERE Orders.customer_id = Customers.id)
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Customers WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Orders WHERE Orders.customer_id = Customers.id);

title: Departments With Employees
prompt: Find departments that have at least one employee assigned.
hint: Use EXISTS with a correlated subquery: WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Employees WHERE Employees.department_id = Departments.id)
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM Departments WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Employees WHERE Employees.department_id = Departments.id);

title: Products Not Ordered

title: Delete and Insert

expectedQuery: DELETE FROM Inventory WHERE supplier_id = 3; INSERT INTO Inventory VALUES(1, 3, 100);

title: Archival Pattern
prompt: Create an 'OldOrders' table with same structure as Orders, move orders from before March 2024 into it, then delete them from Orders.

title: Temp Table
prompt: Create a temporary table 'TempSales' with product_id (INTEGER) and total_qty (INTEGER).

title: Complex CHECK
prompt: Create a table 'Events' with: id (PK), start_date (TEXT), end_date (TEXT), with CHECK that end_date > start_date.

expectedQuery: CREATE TABLE Events (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, start_date TEXT NOT NULL, end_date TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK (end_date > start_date));

title: Compound Index
prompt: Create a compound index 'idx_sales_product_date' on SalesLog covering product_id and sale_date.

expectedQuery: CREATE INDEX idx_sales_product_date ON SalesLog(product_id, sale_date);

title: Table with Foreign Key
prompt: Create a table 'OrderItems' with: id (PK), order_id (INTEGER REFERENCES Orders(id)), product_id (INTEGER), qty (INTEGER).
hint: REFERENCES creates a foreign key: column_name INTEGER REFERENCES table(column). Enable with PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON.
expectedQuery: CREATE TABLE OrderItems (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, order_id INTEGER REFERENCES Orders(id), product_id INTEGER, qty INTEGER);

title: Create Table IF NOT EXISTS
prompt: Create a table 'AuditLog' only if it doesn't already exist: id (PK), action (TEXT), timestamp (TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP).

expectedQuery: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS AuditLog (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, action TEXT, timestamp TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP);

title: Drop and Recreate

title: After Insert Trigger
prompt: Create a trigger 'log_new_employee' that inserts into AuditLog when a new employee is added. First create AuditLog, then the trigger.
hint: CREATE TRIGGER name AFTER INSERT ON table BEGIN ... END; — NEW.column references the inserted row's values.
expectedQuery: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS AuditLog (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, action TEXT, timestamp TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP); CREATE TRIGGER log_new_employee AFTER INSERT ON Employees BEGIN INSERT INTO AuditLog(action) VALUES('New employee: ' || NEW.name); END;

title: Before Update Trigger
prompt: Create a trigger that prevents salary decreases: raise an error if new salary < old salary.

expectedQuery: CREATE TRIGGER prevent_salary_decrease BEFORE UPDATE ON Employees BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'Salary cannot be decreased') WHERE NEW.salary < OLD.salary; END;
verificationQuery: SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='trigger' AND name='prevent_salary_decrease';

title: Auto-Audit Trigger
prompt: Create a trigger that logs salary changes to EmployeeHistory automatically when Employees is updated.
hint: AFTER UPDATE trigger with OLD and NEW: INSERT INTO EmployeeHistory VALUES(NULL, OLD.id, OLD.salary, NEW.salary, DATE('now'));

verificationQuery: SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='trigger' AND name='salary_audit';

title: Drop Trigger
prompt: Drop the trigger 'salary_audit' if it exists.
hint: DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trigger_name; — safely removes a trigger without error if it doesn't exist.
starterCode:
-- First create it, then drop it
CREATE TRIGGER salary_audit AFTER UPDATE OF salary ON Employees BEGIN INSERT INTO EmployeeHistory(employee_id, old_salary, new_salary, change_date) VALUES(OLD.id, OLD.salary, NEW.salary, DATE('now')); END;
expectedQuery: CREATE TRIGGER salary_audit AFTER UPDATE OF salary ON Employees BEGIN INSERT INTO EmployeeHistory(employee_id, old_salary, new_salary, change_date) VALUES(OLD.id, OLD.salary, NEW.salary, DATE('now')); END; DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS salary_audit;
verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='trigger' AND name='salary_audit';

title: Partial Index

title: json_object

prompt: In a single transaction: insert a new department (6, 'Legal') and a new employee (13, 'Nina', 60000, 6, '2024-06-01', 'nina@company.com', NULL).

prompt: In a transaction: 1) Create a 'EmployeeTags' table (employee_id INT, tag TEXT), 2) Insert tags for employee 1: 'senior' and 'lead'.
